data.summary: Take-over claim refused as 'queued behind <waiter>' is not approval-overrideable: ddflow claim <id> --approval request returns exit 3 and files nothing. When an agent re-claims an item whose lease is held by a paused/other lane, and an earlier --queue waiter overlaps some of the item's globs, the 'queued' claim guard (claim_guard_queued.py, order 20) fires first and its refusal reason names neither '--force' nor '--approval request', so claim()'s _names_claim_override() returns the raw refusal without routing to _claim_by_approval (the operator's take-over route). --break cannot reach the lease either (the guard fires before _acquire; ClaimContext.skip honours only force/held_before, not break_lease). Repro: ddflow --agent tkl-verify claim VR-verify-filed --approval request -> exit 3, 'queued behind lane-lock (lock-fold-outside)', ddflow approvals pending -> 'no approval requests pending'. Same class as Be62e44611e (foreign-expired-lease refusal) but that fix only marked the expired-lease refusal, not the queued guard.
data.title: queued claim guard refusal drops the --approval request take-over route

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B577d271d24 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B577d271d24 --regression-test <test>` first).
